title: Contractor
summary: A 2014 contractor column contrasts an old heat pump running on resistance backup in a cold winter with an efficient mini-split retrofit replacing baseboard heat.

assertions.quote: you heat your home with those resistive electric elements — the most expensive way to heat
Elizabeth's heat pump ran as a straight-electric heater for many weeks this past winter

verdicts.note: Heat pumps sized for cooling rely on electric resistance heat when the heat pump alone cannot meet the heating load.
Edwards notes that air-source heat pumps become markedly less efficient in extreme cold, where dual-fuel or resistance backup has traditionally been used, though two-stage units reduce the need.
With much of Minnesota below -10F design temperature, the heat pump is unlikely to meet the full load at all temperatures, making a backup heat source necessary.
Even Manual-J-sized cold-climate prototypes showed a common need for some auxiliary support at 0-10 F at several sites, though it was a small fraction of total output.
Despite better cold-weather performance, a backup system may still be needed in parts of Canada to keep a home warm in the coldest periods, and insurers often require one.

assertions.quote: Next year's energy bills, for this young family of three, will be slashed dramatically.
without the need for any back-up heating and do so at outdoor temperatures well below 0°F
The DHW is now being frugally produced with a heat pump water heater

verdicts.note: RMI models heat pump water heaters at a COP of 2.53-2.64 against 0.59-0.62 for gas, oil and propane water heaters, about four times the delivered heat per unit of energy.
LBNL: installed electric heat pump water heaters had a median Energy Factor of 3.15, compared with all other water heater types below 1.0 (rated efficiency, not metered use).
